strip: # pnl-motor-starter 0.5 · the terminal plan (lib/panel-shop.md "Out"; role card r2; arrangement: NFPA 79 13.1 as the card cites it: view-only and not read into a table so no wording of it is quoted here).

# strip.terminal is the number on the marker (X1:1 .. X1:24 and PE:1 .. PE:6); tag is the block's BOM tag; its pins are tag.1 and tag.2 (term-4mm behaviour.csv: clamp-1 and clamp-2 joined by the current bar).

# side1 = clamp 1 (the block's top entry: toward the rails and duct-1085); side2 = clamp 2 (the bottom entry: toward duct-790 and the gland plate). The panel's devices land on side 1; what leaves the panel lands on side 2.
# One conductor a clamp (the shop's design rule: how many conductors one clamp of term-4mm may take is not in its brief). So a potential with more than two ends is a bridged group of blocks:
# bridge names the group; the bridge itself is term-jumper (request panel-3 item 1): since 0.12 term-jumper 2.0 placed
terminal: one comb a group (bom.csv jmp-1 on X1:1 to 4 · jmp-2 on X1:5 to 8 · jmp-3 on X1:15 and 16; wires.csv joins blade k to the k-th block). To 0.11 the groups were planned and not built.

strip: # The PE blocks are common through their bonding feet and rail-4 (term-4mm spec: ground block with a metal bonding foot); the rail's rating as that conductor is NOT ON FILE (B): IEC 60947-7-2 (spec.md section 7).

# wire: wires.csv's numbers (0.5) as <side 1's wire>/<side 2's wire>; a side with no wire yet is blank; a number in brackets is kept for a wire whose other end is not on file; a bracketed lead (0.10: (w-pwr.B1)) is a cordset's own conductor landed there
terminal: not a wire the shop cuts. status: planned (both ends on file) · reserved (one end waits on an answer) · spare.
2026-11-11): the controller's four signals leave by three A-coded wall ports of the panel (p-x4 to io-1 port-x3 · p-x5 to port-x4 · p-x6 to port-x7)
tag: each input contact fed from that port's own pin 1 (U_S) and back to pin 4 or 2
side1: never from the panel's bus (answer 3.c); the run output (port-x7 pin 4) sources K1's coil chain (3.a); the overload signals the trip on 97-98 while 95-96 stays in the coil chain (3.d: the point is ol_trip).

strip: # What has no terminal: the supply's phases land on q1 L1 L2 L3 (the spec's supply row); f1 T1 T2 T3 go to the receptacle p-m1's own terminals (X1 is the control strip; no power strip in the BOM);

# the Ethernet link is the cordset w-eth from plc-1 port-eth to p-x1's pigtail (0.7: bom.csv; a data pair is not broken at a screw terminal: a design choice); the panel's own circuits (the K1 coil chain between f1 95-96 and k-safe 13 · the safety relay's S11 and S21 to the door e-stop · the transformer and the PSU's input) go device to device (role card r2).
